## Summary
The canonical JSON format option works on successful reads but does not select JSON for failures. A consumer can parse success and then fail to parse the same command's error.

Reproduced with the official installed `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.9.30 on Linux, using disposable synthetic non-Git trackers. No implementation changes are included in this issue.

## Reproduction
```bash
LAB=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$LAB/home" "$LAB/work"
export HOME="$LAB/home" PM_PATH="$LAB/work/.agents/pm"
export PM_GLOBAL_PATH="$LAB/global" PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
cd "$LAB/work"
pm init "$PM_PATH" --defaults --author audit --agent-guidance skip --json >/dev/null
pm create task "Audit sample" --id t1 --description "Execution detail" --json >/dev/null
```
```bash
pm get pm-t1 --output-format json
pm get pm-missing --output-format json 2>error.txt
pm get pm-missing --output-format=json 2>error-attached.txt
pm get pm-missing --json 2>error.json
pm create task "Format test" --priority bad --output-format json
pm search x --limit bad --output-format json
```

## Actual
- Successful get returns JSON
- Both spellings of `--output-format json` on missing get exit 3 with human stderr beginning `Error: Item ID not found`
- The equivalent `--json` failure returns structured JSON stderr
- Invalid create priority and search limit also emit human diagnostics under `--output-format json`

## Expected and impact
Equivalent advertised JSON selectors select the same format on success and failure. Preserve the exit code and stderr error channel, but keep that channel machine-parseable. An agent should not need a second, undocumented formatting flag to recover safely.

## Implementation plan
1. Use one output-format resolver for normal results and diagnostics, with explicit precedence for aliases, attached values and conflicting selectors.
2. Resolve enough format context before validation/dispatch that early failures use the requested format too.
3. Keep JSON error streams free of human prefixes or incidental diagnostics.
4. Document output and error channel guarantees and test the packed executable, not only serializer units.

## Regression acceptance
- [ ] Matrix: `--json`, `--output-format json`, `--output-format=json`, supported aliases, and supported default/config modes
- [ ] Matrix: success, item-not-found, invalid value, unknown flag, missing argument and policy refusal
- [ ] Every JSON error stream parses as one JSON value and includes the unchanged typed code/exit status
- [ ] Flags before/after command and conflicting-format precedence are deterministic
- [ ] Human/TOON diagnostic paths retain their intended behavior

## Ownership and duplicate check
Child of #1363; shared CLI contract coverage for #1362. Closed #1271 concerned rejection of output-format on mutations; this issue is failure serialization, reproduced on an ordinary read as well. Searched open and closed output-format/error reports; no exact open owner found.
GH-1366: Agent UX: --output-format json emits human errors while --json emits structured errors

Reported agent-facing contract defect imported from https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1366. Preserve existing shipped foundations. Detailed source observations are dated 2026-09-30 and must be revalidated before implementation.

Matrix: `--json`, `--output-format json`, `--output-format=json`, supported aliases, and supported default/config modes; Matrix: success, item-not-found, invalid value, unknown flag, missing argument and policy refusal; Every JSON error stream parses as one JSON value and includes the unchanged typed code/exit status; Flags before/after command and conflicting-format precedence are deterministic; Human/TOON diagnostic paths retain their intended behavior
The public command follows the documented equivalent-option, receipt or recovery contract without changing valid unrelated behavior.
Source report reproduced published 2026.9.30 behavior; current checkout requires fresh reproduction before claiming the defect.
